narrative.overview: A dark, quiet working surface where data is the only thing that shines. Every panel reads like a page of a lab notebook: a numbered title, a one-line note on what is measured and how, the chart or table, then a short reading of the result. Nothing on screen is decorative; colour, weight and position all carry meaning. The system is dense but calm. Slate layers separate regions instead of shadows, a single blue accent marks interaction, and semantic colours (market identity, rise/fall, forecast) are reserved for data. Typography is one sans family; numbers switch to monospace so columns line up and read as measurements. Refinement keeps this world: tighten consistency, legibility on a projector-free laptop and on a phone, and the "note under every chart" habit.
keyCharacteristics: Dark slate layering (page → panel → inset), flat, bordered.
One interactive accent (blue); data colours never double as UI colours.
Numbered panel titles with a source/method subtitle.
Monospace numerals for every measured value.
Each chart ends with a one-line plain-Vietnamese reading.

rules.name: The One Market, One Colour Rule
rules.body: Stock is always Stock Blue and crypto always Copper Crypto, in charts, badges and legends alike. A filter never repaints a series.

rules.name: The Accent Is For Hands Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue means "you can act here". Data that happens to be blue uses Stock Blue in a chart context, never on a control.

rules.name: The Measured Number Rule
rules.body: Any value computed from data is set in monospace with its unit; prose never carries a bare number without its unit or period.

rules.name: The Layer Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: New surfaces separate by tone and border, never by adding shadows.

dos: Do number panel titles and give each a subtitle naming the method or source.
Do end every chart panel with a one-line reading of what it shows.
Do keep Stock Blue (`#3B82F6`) and Copper Crypto (`#D97706`) identical across charts, badges and legends.
Do draw forecast lines dashed in Forecast Amber (`#F59E0B`) and keep the Naive baseline visible next to any model result.
Do set measured values in monospace with units.
donts: Don't use Signal Blue on data or semantic colours on controls.
Don't add shadows, gradients or glows to separate surfaces.
Don't rely on colour alone: every multi-series chart has a legend or direct labels.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or a warm grey into the slate neutrals.
